items.label: SPY5 + SPYL (S&P 500 duplication)
items.detail: SPY5 ($223,473.60, 45.65% of NAV) and SPYL ($119,857.92, 24.48% of NAV) both track the S&P 500 and together total $343,331.52 = 70.13% of the $489,544.45 NAV (source: get_account_positions, get_account_summary, live 2026-08-31). Computed 1-year daily-return correlation between the two is 0.9929 (n=252, get_price_history closes Aug 2025-Aug 2026).
items.recommendation: Trim SPYL (the smaller, more redundant leg) by roughly half -- approx. 3,120 of 6,240 shares (~$59,929 at the $19.208 last price) -- and redeploy into SHY (iShares 1-3Y Treasury), which showed the lowest correlation to both SPY5 (-0.0402) and SPYL (-0.0456) of six hedge candidates tested (IEF +0.087, TLT +0.113, AGG +0.150, EFA +0.463, VXUS +0.498).

items.label: Zero fixed-income ballast ahead of a hawkish Fed repricing
items.detail: get_pa_allocation (live) shows 0% of NAV in bonds -- allocation is 81.0% ETFs (equity/commodity), 13.1% direct equities, 5.9% cash, with no duration exposure anywhere. Chase Wealth Management now expects a 25bp Fed rate HIKE at the Sept 15-16, 2026 FOMC meeting (reversing prior rate-cut expectations), citing Iran-conflict energy shocks keeping inflation elevated; the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.32% on Aug 18, 2026 -- its highest since early 2024 -- triggering a broad selloff in rate-sensitive growth names that day (sources: chase.com Sept-2026 rate outlook; Motley Fool/CNBC Aug 18 2026 market reports).
items.recommendation: Establish a Treasury ballast (SHY and/or IEF) sized at roughly 5% of NAV (~$24,500); both showed near-zero to low correlation to the account's largest equity holding (SHY -0.04, IEF +0.09 vs SPY5), making them the most effective portfolio-level shock absorbers identified in this analysis.

items.label: Available trading funds ($208.72) vs. reported cash balance ($28,311.97)
items.detail: get_account_summary (live) reports total_cash_value $28,311.97 (5.78% of NAV) but available_funds and buying_power of only $208.72; excess_liquidity is separately reported at $28,311.97 -- an inconsistency in the raw IBKR data worth confirming directly in the platform before placing new orders.
items.recommendation: Verify true buying power in the IBKR client before funding any hedge position with fresh cash. If available funds are genuinely near-zero, fund the SHY/TLT/IEF additions recommended here by trimming SPYL and/or the gold cluster rather than deploying new capital.

items.detail: IGLN ($41,294.48, 8.43%), SSLV ($7,771.48, 1.59%), KGC ($5,341.00, 1.09%) and NEM ($5,896.15, 1.20%) total $60,303.11 = 12.32% of NAV (get_account_positions, live). Gold traded near $4,380/oz in mid-August 2026 (Yahoo Finance/JPMorgan reporting), its strongest monthly gain since January's record run; the next major catalysts are the Sept 10 CPI print and the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting, where hike odds have risen materially (sources: chase.com, goldsilver.com, Aug 2026).

items.detail: CRWV ($12,490.50, 2.55% of NAV, -$311.50 unrealized, -$144.00 today) and GEV ($8,918.30, 1.82% of NAV, -$830.60 unrealized, -$200.99 today) sold off together on Aug 18, 2026 (CRWV -12.10%, GEV roughly -6%, per Motley Fool/CNBC) when the 30-year yield spiked to 5.32% and Middle East tensions resurfaced -- despite CRWV beating Q2 revenue estimates with +112% YoY growth that same week. items.recommendation: Trim CRWV specifically (the pair's higher-volatility, debt-financing-cost-sensitive leg) by 30-50%, or lean on the SHY/IEF Treasury ballast above -- both showed low correlation to the account's broad equity factor in this analysis.

diversification_actions.action: Fund a SHY (iShares 1-3Y Treasury) position by trimming roughly half of SPYL

diversification_actions.action: Layer in IEF (iShares 7-10Y Treasury) alongside SHY as a complementary intermediate-duration hedge
diversification_actions.rationale: IEF's 1-year correlation to SPY5 (+0.087) and SPYL (+0.087) is the second-lowest of six candidates tested, well below EFA (+0.46/+0.45) and VXUS (+0.50/+0.49); pairing SHY's near-zero correlation with IEF's longer duration spreads the equity hedge across more of the yield curve instead of concentrating it in one maturity bucket.
